summary: Jacques André worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology after studying at the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He held positions at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, served as president of the Société Asiatique (1945–1954), and taught at the University of Paris.

Jacques Gernet studied at the University of Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE, working in sinology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at EPHE, the University of Paris, Paris Diderot University, and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

Jacques Giès was a specialist in sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at Paris-Sorbonne University under Flora Blanchon. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne and École du Louvre, and served as president of the Musée Guimet (2008–2011).

Jacques Leider specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at INALCO under Denise Bernot and Pierre L. Lamant, taught at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999), and became a maître de conférences at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient in 2001.

Jacques May was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as editor-in-chief for Hōbōgirin and at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~1964–1981), and was a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1978–1992).

Jacques Scheuer works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at UCLouvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau, and served on the faculties of Centre Sèvres and UCLouvain (~1980–2007).

Jadunath Sarkar was an Indian historian educated at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. He held academic posts at Patna College (1899–1926) and Ravenshaw University, and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).

Jagdish Kashyap was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology educated at Patna College, Banaras Hindu University, and Vidyalankara Pirivena. He taught Pali at Banaras Hindu University, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and served as director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jaideva Singh worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Srikrishna Harihirlekar and Nankoo Bhaya Telang. He served as chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and was Chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1973.

Jake H. Davis is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from CUNY. He has held positions at Brown University, the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies, and NYU.

Jakob Steiner studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Berlin. He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Applied Sciences Berlin (1825–1834) and Frederick William University Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Oxford and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He held professorial chairs at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and the University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, having studied at Cambridge, SOAS under Timothy H. Barrett, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He has held posts at Lewis & Clark College and McMaster University.
James Adam was a scholar of philosophy who completed his studies at the University of Aberdeen (~1876–1880) and Gonville and Caius College (~1880–1884).

James Alan Matisoff is a scholar of linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology who studied at Harvard and UC Berkeley. He taught at Columbia University (1966–1969) and was a professor of linguistics at the University of California, Berkeley (1970–2002).

James Atkinson was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar educated at the University of Edinburgh. He held positions at the India Government Mint in Kolkata and served as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.

James B. Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his graduate studies and PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under John D. Dunne, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and numerous other teachers.

James Blumenthal was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He held faculty posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.

James Burgess was a scholar of Indology and archaeology who studied at the universities of Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1886–1889) and Vice President of the Royal Society of Edinburgh (1908–1914).
